paragraphs: Friend, here's what this passage is really about. Jehu wipes Baal out of Israel, and the LORD says he "has done well in carrying out what is right in My sight" (2 Kings 10:30). But the writer won't let us stop there. Jehu "did not turn away from the sins that Jeroboam had caused Israel to commit" (2 Kings 10:31).

So here's the lesson: you can get a BIG job done for the LORD and still keep a small thing you won't let go of. Jehu cleaned out the temple and left the golden calves standing at Bethel and Dan (2 Kings 10:29). The text says he "was not careful to follow the instruction of the LORD, the God of Israel, with all his heart" (2 Kings 10:31). I think that's the part to sit with. Obeying with all your heart means the whole job, not just the loud parts.

Now, this doesn't mean the LORD missed the good. He promised Jehu that four generations of his sons would sit on the throne (2 Kings 10:30), and that promise is right there in the text. Still, in those days the LORD began to reduce the size of Israel (2 Kings 10:32). So ask yourself, baker: what's my golden calf, the thing I keep saying I'll deal with later? I've got a whole oven full of mercy for you, and I'm telling you now, it's better to hand it over to the LORD than to keep it in the back of the drawer.
